title: Not This Time
story:
At nine fifty-eight on Thursday, I join the call. My glass of water sits beside the laptop. Outside our apartment, someone is moving a chair across the floor.

Sara appears on the screen at ten.

“Thank you for making time, Andy.”

“Thank you for speaking with me.”

She does not spend long on small talk.

“We've decided not to take your application forward.”

I look at the small picture of myself in the corner. My face hardly changes.

“Okay,” I say.

Sara explains that the role involves frequent calls with customers. The team needs someone who can lead those discussions from the start. They are not confident that I am ready for that part of this particular role.

“We did see useful technical experience,” she adds. “Your explanation of the stock problem was clear.”

I had prepared questions, but now they seem to belong to a different person. I take a drink of water.

“Can I ask about the project example?”

“Of course.”

“Was the example wrong, or was my explanation difficult to follow?”

“The example was relevant. But it took us some time to understand your part and the result. A shorter structure would help.”

I write ‘my part’ and ‘result’ on the paper in front of me.

“And the customer question?”

“You answered before you fully understood it. You corrected that when Ben repeated it. In a customer call, checking the question earlier would be important.”

Her voice is calm. I want to explain how nervous I was, but that will not change what they heard.

“Thank you,” I say. “That's useful to know.”

We end the call after twelve minutes. I close the laptop, then open it again to save my notes. The kitchen is quiet now. Even the chair upstairs has stopped moving.

For lunch, I cook rice and an egg. I eat standing by the counter until I notice what I am doing. Then I take the bowl to the table.

In the afternoon, Rui calls.

“I didn't get it,” I tell him.

“I'm sorry.”

“They need someone who can lead customer calls now.”

“That makes sense for some roles.”

I do not want it to make sense. I want him to say they are wrong. But he waits, and I tell him the rest of the feedback.

Then he says, “I have some news too. I've accepted a job at Northstar.”

For a second, I say nothing. We were looking for work at the same time, but he already has a place to go.

“That's great,” I say. It is true, even if another feeling sits beside it. “When do you start?”

“Next week. I went through the interviews last month.”

He tells me about the engineering team and the trip to the office. I ask a few questions. Our call becomes easier.

After we hang up, I open the message where he told me he was thinking about moving. I count back from his start date. He must have been waiting for his own news when he asked how my interview went. I never asked how his went.

I pick up the phone again. I want to send him something big and cheerful. What comes out is smaller. ‘I forgot to ask. Is the journey to the new place any better?’

‘One train,’ he replies. ‘A seat if the whole city stays home.’

On Friday I try the report story on my phone. I press record and put the phone across the table. The first time, I hear myself say “we” six times. In the middle there's a long minute about the company. I would turn me off too.

The next recording is so short that the shop manager disappears. On the third try I give him one sentence. I listen while I wash my bowl. I can hear what the man needed, what I changed, and which part another person did. I save that one.

On Monday morning my phone shows a picture from Rui. His new desk has three screens and no chair yet. Under it he writes, ‘Standing job.’

I laugh before I remember to feel sorry for myself. I send a picture of my kitchen chair. ‘Very good chair. Expensive delivery.’

Two weeks later, he sends me a link to an open software role there. By then, I have sent more applications and practised several work examples aloud.

‘This is a different position from mine,’ his message says. ‘You should read the requirements. I can't promise anything.’

I open the link. The role includes team discussions in English and some client contact with support from a project lead. It also asks for experience I already have.

That evening, I tell Maya about it while we clear the table.

“Are you applying?” she asks.

“Yes. But I'm checking the role carefully first.”

She hands me a dry plate. I put it in the cupboard, then return for the next one. My laptop waits at the far end of the table, with the new advertisement still open.

When the plates are away, I go back to the part about client calls. I read the little word ‘with’ twice. At Meridian they needed somebody to lead those calls immediately. Here a project lead goes too. I open a fresh application. In the box about working with customers I write about the shop manager and his Monday numbers. I leave Rui's name out of that box. He wasn't there.

phrases.en: Can I ask about the project example?
My explanation was difficult to follow.
I’m checking the role carefully first.
phrases.zh: 说明行动前要核对岗位要求

practice.grammar: 用 because 连接决定与原因：The role is difficult for me because it involves frequent customer calls. 原因应来自已知反馈，不替他人猜测动机。
practice.pronunciation: 朗读 Was the example WRONG, / or was my explanation difficult to FOLLOW? 两个选项之间停顿，重读 wrong 和 follow，让请求反馈的重点清楚。

questions.q: Why does Meridian decide not to take Andy forward?
questions.a: The role needs someone ready to lead frequent customer calls, and the team is not confident Andy is ready for that part.

questions.q: What does Andy notice when he listens to his first recording?
questions.a: He keeps saying “we” and spends too long explaining the company.

questions.q: When does Rui send the Northstar role to Andy?
questions.a: He sends it two weeks after the rejection call, after starting work there.

roleplay.context: 你扮演 Andy，收到拒信后与招聘人员沟通。

turns.line: We have decided not to move forward.
turns.cue: 简短回应，询问是否可以请教一个具体问题。

turns.line: Your project answer was hard to follow.
turns.cue: 追问是例子不合适还是贡献与结果不清楚。

turns.line: We needed more detail about your own work.
turns.cue: 确认改进重点并感谢反馈。

practice.transfer: 换到一次未被采用的工作建议：向负责人提出两个具体的反馈问题。开口练习接受一个不喜欢但有用的回答，不为自己作长篇辩解。
practice.retell: 用一分钟复述拒绝理由、两条反馈、Rui 的消息和 Andy 的下一步。区分 Meridian 与 Northstar，不把岗位链接说成录用。
